reading:
Settled Light is the lineage's best carrier (tour 7.22, landing 7.61, #4 of 16). What the judges love: Home as a sommaire, a map of the whole service where every page is a cell with its count (usability: "best for finding your way"; skeptic: "the best whole-service idea here, which the main tournament should adopt"); the household index row along Home's foot; the contents typesetting ("Plans ........ 4 coming", with a large light figure and a small unit word, and stacked day numerals); the small radar scope beside the plan rows it numbers; and above all the light. Soul gave 8.3 because it "puts the most tube back of any final": the question typed on green glass, and every inner page's own small sized tube (the To do ASCII tally, the plans weekend screen, the spend screen) at full halo, scanlines and breathing lamps, on matte ground. System calls the inner rack "the most transferable page template here".

What sank it: (1) The title. "What's the plan?" reads as "show me the plan" to every lens, and in VT323 the apostrophe takes a whole cell. It is small mono inside the glass, so the one action loses rank (interaction, type, usability). (2) Materials. The graphite case round the greeting is "a heavy slab" (feedback) and "a greyed graphite slab, i.e. a tinted ground" (skeptic). The panels are boxes in boxes (system) and come close to stock dark mode (style). The box reads as a display, not a field (usability), and its inner glow is the largest green area (soul). (3) Almost no line art (feedback, twice). (4) The inner rack is repetitive: short lists float beside a 22rem column, the chat has a dead left column, To do leaves empty graphite, and Chat's box is one line. (5) Small things: amber late checkboxes shout, two kind inks in Ideas, faint leaders, stacked full-width starter slabs, setup leading the right column, and one or two targets under 44px.

What would make it win: keep the map and the light split exactly as they are, and fix the title and the materials. Do that by taking what the main camp does best. From Desk Terminal, Joined (8.33, the leader): its head row on every page, its lit NOW rail and tick, and its moving-coil meter. From Quote Board: its quote head (condensed title, figure in the section ink, a stacked unit and change line), which is exactly the head a sommaire cell wants. With those the switchboard gets real hierarchy and line art without losing its identity. The sheet is at 191.8k of the 200k budget, so the cross must trim before it adds.

briefs.name: Switchboard, Quoted
briefs.hypothesis: Settled Light already has the tournament's best map (the sommaire Home with its household index) and its truest light (a small sized tube per page). It lost points only on rank and material: a small mono title that reads 'show me', a graphite slab and boxes in boxes, no line art, and an inner rack that floats. The main camp's leader solved exactly these with a head row, a lit NOW rail and a meter, and Quote Board solved the head with its quote device. Grafted into the switchboard's own ink and leaders, they give the map a type hierarchy and line art. The light stays where the soul judges put it, and nothing of the line's idea is lost. That should lift system, interaction, type and skeptic by about a point each while holding soul at 8+.
briefs.brief:
START from t3-switchboard-refine (sheet.css, templates/*, static/icons.svg). BUDGET FIRST: the sheet is 191.8k of 200k. Rebuild it from tools/parts so that the later layers (g_settled.css, h_light.css, f_revise.css, e_graft.css) are folded into the rules they override, not stacked on top of them. Delete what this brief removes (the case slab, the plate rules, the 2-column kind key grid, the Home inner box glow). Get under 182k before adding anything, and finish under 197k.

TOKENS (kept, plus a few). The ground stays near-black green (--bg). Panels LOSE their graphite fill: .cell, .hh and .rack become transparent on --bg, with a 1px --line edge (#2a312e) and one 2px cap in their section ink (sky --plans, sea --todo, bone for the household, pewter for Ideas). New tokens: --leader: #48524d (a step brighter than today's line-2, which type, style and usability asked for); --cord: #5b6a72 (steel, for the patch lines); --well: #0a0d0c (the field's matte well); --hot: color-mix(in srgb,#6dff9c 45%,#fff) (white-hot). Bright #6dff9c only on the mark, Send and the primaries, the title's lit word and its cursor, lamps, focus, the NOW tick and rail stretch, and the tubes. Green share targets: Home ≤ 48%, Chat ≤ 55%.

TYPE SYSTEM, in steps. IBM Plex Sans Condensed 600 for every title and head: page title 2.5rem/1.05, cell head 1.625rem. Plex Sans for body at 1.0625rem, and rows at 1.1875rem/600. Plex Mono only for figures in columns (times, 'in 2 days') with tabular-nums. VT323 only on glass. Unit words are sentence-case Plex Mono 0.8125rem in pewter, never tracked caps. text-wrap: balance on heads and pretty on paragraphs. Nothing on a page under 0.8125rem (type asked for the 'Lately added' meta and 'Each mark is a plan' to reach the floor).

HOME (the sommaire, two tiers kept):
1. THE GREETING. Drop .case's graphite slab and inset (feedback, skeptic). The terminal is now the glass alone in a fine 1px steel bezel (--bezel-hi top edge, --bezel-lo foot, 10px radius), standing on the page's own black, the only lit, rounded surface on Home. Make the glass taller and wider (system: 'a real screen on Home'). Its top line is Vera's screen glyph, 'Vera' and the date in VT323 1.3rem at --phosphor-dim. Under it is the TITLE as the page's headline (interaction: 'display face at headline size', usability: 'Plex at full bone, only the key word in VT323 green'): 'Give Vera something to' in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at 2.75rem in bone (--here-ink #f3f1ea), then 'plan.' in VT323 at 3.6rem (matched to the condensed cap height) in #6dff9c with the kit's three-layer halo (0 0 2px, 0 0 10px, 0 0 28px at .35), and a breathing block cursor after it. It has no apostrophe, so VT323's gap is gone. Under the title is the BOX as the glass's last rows: a matte --well field with a 1px #3a4440 edge, Plex Sans 1.0625rem bone text, a pewter placeholder and a green '>' prompt glyph at the left. It is 3 rows tall, with NO inner glow (soul: halve it; here it is removed and the light kept on the title and caret). Focus gives a 2px #6dff9c ring and a faint 0 0 18px bloom. Below the glass is a slim key ledge: From, mic, 'Send where I am', and Send (the green primary).
2. THE STARTERS. One left-aligned row of three keys, the column's own edge (type), with sentence-case labels at 0.9375rem/600, each 52px tall. Under each label is its destination as a patch tag in Plex Mono 0.8125rem pewter: '→ Plans', '→ To do', '→ Ideas' (interaction, system and style all asked for Patched Through's tags). On hover and focus the matching map cell's head lamp lights green (a :has() selector on .map). On the phone they wrap to two rows; all three and 'Continue with Vera' stay on the first screen (soul, style, usability).
3. SETUP becomes a one-line strip across the full width above the two tiers (interaction): an amber 8px lamp, 'Finish setting up' in condensed 600, a dotted --leader, the next step as the link ('Choose your own password →'), then 'then Telegram, Google Calendar' in pewter and 'All 3 steps' at the right. The strip is 56px tall with a 2px amber left edge on --bg, not a panel.
4. MAP CELLS (right tier: Plans and To do a step larger; Ideas under the glass). Each cell head is a QUOTE HEAD (graft): the condensed title, a patch cord, then the figure, then a stacked unit and change line (see BORROWS). Plans: 'Plans', then the figure '4', then 'coming' over 'next in 2 days'. To do: 'To do', '4', then 'open' over '3 late' (the late figure in amber words, linked). Ideas: '12', then 'saved' over 'last added Sun'.
5. PLANS CELL. Keep the small radar scope at the left, now with no case: a 1px steel ring bezel. Beside it, Desk Terminal's NOW RAIL runs down the left of the day numerals: a 1px --cord rail, a white-hot NOW lamp with a 'Now' label at its top, a 2px lit #6dff9c stretch from NOW to the first plan's ring, and steel rings at the other plans. Keep the stacked day numerals (sky light 2.25rem, weekday and month stacked). Show the month in the cell foot ('October' in bone) (interaction).
6. TO DO CELL. Checkboxes are neutral (a 1.5px #5d6a72 outline in a 44px hit square, skeptic, twice); late shows as amber words plus a 2px amber tick at the row's left edge. Desk's lit NOW TICK sits between the late rows and the rest. The cell ends with its rows (align-self:start; grid-auto-rows:min-content), and under the last row a 'Next due' or 'Oldest late: Call the dentist about Theo, 5 days' line closes it, so no empty graphite is left (style, type, usability, interaction).
7. IDEAS CELL. Kind words in one ink (pewter) and kind icons in their kind ink (skeptic: one ink, not teal plus amber).
8. HOUSEHOLD INDEX (the foot row: Wishes, Memory, Family, Status, Settings). More darkspace above it (3rem; soul). Cells are 6rem tall, each a contents line (head, --leader, a large light figure, a small unit), and each head has a lamp: a dim pinhole normally, a steady green lamp where it is live (Status 'answering'), and on Settings alone an amber lamp that breathes once every 2.4s where it needs a look (soul: 'light only the one that needs a look'). Memory keeps 'Tell Vera something →' rather than a faked count.

INNER PAGES (one rack, now varied):
9. A HEAD ROW on every inner page (graft), full width above the rack: the page icon, then the quote head ('Things to do' 4 open / 3 late; 'Plans' 5 in October / next Sun 4, 13:00; 'Ideas' 12 saved / 2 restaurants to try; 'Status' $1.26 in 30 days / 6 calls; 'Vera' over her one-line lede), the lede on one balanced line under it (max 56ch), and the page's one green primary at the right ('Add something to do', 'Add an idea', 'Connect the calendar'). The old plate leaves the rack.
10. THE RACK is now only the tube and the controls, at 19rem (was 22rem), so the list column widens (system, skeptic). The tube sits first and the filters below it as latched keys. Ideas' kind filter becomes one wrapping chip row of 44px keys (system). To do adds 'Late' to Show (usability). On Plans and To do the list column starts level with the tube's top, so nothing floats.
11. TO DO's tube keeps its ASCII tally (late, this week, later, no date) but its last line names the news (soul, interaction): 'Next: Renew library cards' in white-hot when something is dated ahead, or otherwise 'Oldest late: Call the dentist, 5 d', with the Late row's blocks amber on the glass. The list gets the same neutral checkboxes and NOW tick as Home.
12. PLANS month: hairline cells only (drop the boxed fills, feedback). The month name is in the head row's change line. Today keeps its lamp.
13. STATUS: the tube's ASCII bar '[.....] 0%' is replaced by a moving-coil SPEND METER (graft), drawn on settled's glass. The three lamp columns lose their panel fill and keep their caps.
14. CHAT. The thread uses its pane: the composer moves into the thread column as a 3-row matte --well field like Home's (usability: multi-line; system: 'in the column, not across the bottom like a messenger'), with Send beside it. The rack's tube is Vera's small presence screen holding one line, '● Ready' (or 'Working', with the lamp breathing while a turn runs), and under it the kids' conversations as keys, so the left column carries the light and is no longer dead (soul, skeptic). Her newest slip carries the ARRIVED AFTERGLOW (ledger graft below); older slips are matte (#121715 fill, 1px --line edge, no green).
15. SETTINGS, FAMILY, MEMORY, WISHES: the head row too. Their tube folds to one lit line ('● Ready · OpenAI gpt-6-luna · $2.00 a day'). 'Needs a look' is still sorted first.

LIGHT (the kit, kept where it is live): the title word's three-layer halo, scanlines and bloom on every tube, the radar sweep, breathing lamps (only one breathing per page), and row hover afterglow strengthened (soul: it 'fades out almost at once') to a 0.12s light-in and a 1.2s fade on a 2px green left edge and a 6% green wash. prefers-reduced-motion stops the sweep, the breathing and the flash; prefers-contrast:more drops the halos and keeps the solid edges. All targets are 44px or more: probe Home for the last sub-44px target (likely the household roster links 'Maya 0' and 'Theo 0', or 'Sign-in and security'; give them min-block-size 44px with negative block margins).
briefs.borrows:
OWN JUDGES' FIXES, by how many lenses asked:
(a) Title: name the job, lead the page, and avoid VT323's apostrophe. Interaction asked for the display face at headline size; type for a VT323-safe title of at least 40px; usability for Plex at full bone with only the key word in VT323 green; skeptic, landing feedback and every titles verdict said 'What's the plan?' reads as 'show me the plan'. Done in item 1.
(b) The case slab and graphite fills go to the near-black ground with a fine bezel and 1px rules (landing feedback, landing skeptic, tour-3 skeptic; style's 'stock dark mode'; system's 'drop one level of panel nesting'). Items 1 and 4.
(c) Line art (tour-3 and landing feedback): patch cords on cell heads, and the NOW rail (feedback named 'the figure lineage's rail'; it is taken here from Desk Terminal's). Items 4 and 5.
(d) Inner rack: vary it and widen the list (landing style, landing system, tour-3 system, tour-3 skeptic). Items 9 and 10.
(e) To do's empty foot and 'Nothing dated after the late ones' (style, type, usability, interaction, soul). Items 6 and 11.
(f) The box as a field without inner glow (landing usability; tour-3 soul's 'halve it'). Item 1. Chat's composer multi-line and in the column (landing usability and system). Item 14.
(g) Starters as a left-aligned row with destination tags, all of them on the phone (interaction, system, style, type, usability, soul). Item 2.
(h) Setup as a one-line strip (landing interaction). Item 3.
(i) Neutral late checkboxes (tour-3 and landing skeptic). Items 6 and 11.
(j) Household index: more darkspace, larger cells with lamps, and only the needy one lit (landing soul and style, tour-3 soul). Item 8.
(k) Brighter leaders (tour-3 style and type); one kind ink in Ideas (landing skeptic); a kind chip row (landing system); the last sub-44px target (interaction and usability, twice).

OWN LINEAGE, kept: the patch-key destination tags from t3-switchboard-graft Patched Through (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/tour/ ... its _ask.html starters), which five lenses asked for.
briefs.avoids: Every title verdict's 'show me the plan', and the VT323 apostrophe gap (the new title has no apostrophe, and its lead words are in Plex). The 'small mono title loses rank' (interaction): it is now a 2.75rem headline. The 'heavy slab' and 'greyed graphite case' (feedback, skeptic): a bezel on black. 'Boxes in boxes' and 'stock dark mode' (system, style): no fills, one cap, and the plate leaves the rack. 'Almost no line art' (feedback): cords, the NOW rail and the tick. 'Inner pages near-copies and repetitive', 'lists float' and 'dead chat column' (style, system, skeptic): a head row, a narrower rack, the chat composer in the column and a presence tube. To do's 80px empty foot and its uninformative tube line. Amber checkboxes reading as warnings. Two kind inks. Faint leaders. Stacked centred starter slabs, and starters hidden on the phone. Setup leading the right column. A single-line chat box. The last small targets. Green share (the box glow and the case go; target ≤48% on Home). It also avoids the grafts' own known faults: Desk's tracked mono caps and letterspaced 'was due' phrases (here sentence case, with due words in Plex Sans), Quote's numbered bar keys and footer shortcut legend (not taken), Quote's figure far from its label, and Folio's huge folios (no page numbers at all, which already left the line in tour round 3). GIVES UP to make room: the graphite case, the rack's plate (it moves to the head row), the Home box's inner glow, the 2-column kind key grid, Status's ASCII spend bar, the 22rem rack width, and 'What's the plan?'.
briefs.title: Give Vera something to *plan*. This has not been tried yet. It keeps what the panel ranked best in every titles verdict, 'Tell Vera what to plan.': an imperative invitation that names who hears you, with the job word lit at the full stop where the eye lands. 'Something' widens it from the schedule to the family's whole job: an idea to keep, a reminder, a wish and the weekend are all something to hand her to plan. That answers the 'narrower than the whole job' and 'show me the plan' faults of this line's 'What's the plan?'. Nothing about it presumes a plan exists (the fault judges found in 'Tell Vera our plan(s)'), and it cannot be answered 'no' (the fault in 'Anything to plan?'). It has no apostrophe, so it sets cleanly in both of the line's faces: 'Give Vera something to' in Plex Sans Condensed bone, and 'plan.' in VT323 #6dff9c under the full halo, typed on the glass with the cursor after it.
